purpose: Join observed test executions to bounded source assertions; never promote a test name, hit count or draft into a complete rule/card/scenario certification.

expectations.reviewer: skills_audit agent authored mapping, mulligan correction and integration tests; separate root post-implementation signoff is recorded for five bounded integration assertions. Whole scenario completion remains unclaimed.

execution.command: bun test packages/engine/src/engine.test.ts packages/engine/src/combat.test.ts packages/engine/src/integration-scenarios.test.ts packages/simulation/src/driver.test.ts packages/compiler/src/index.test.ts packages/storage/src/storage.test.ts --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=.commander/evidence/core-scenario-map.junit.xml
execution.evidencePolicy: Historical execution. Revalidate test-file hashes and run the current implementation before applying this mapping to a later report. .commander evidence is local and ignored by Git.

guardrails.statement: All 24 separately authored high-risk drafts remain not run; application-contract checks are separated from CR rule assertions. No Bun/browser parity or physical headset claim is derived from this native test report.

discoveredCorrection.before: Bottom selections were delayed until every player kept.
discoveredCorrection.after: Every paid redraw bottoms before the next declaration round; all declarations precede redraw and all bottom decisions precede the next round.

test.name: script lookup is revision-bound and deterministic after retries or reconstruction

assertions: Script driver returns the same response when asked twice at one revision or reconstructed at that revision.
A revision outside the script produces explicit divergence.
limitations: One decision helper; not a full resumed game.

test.name: colored payment reassigns flexible source instead of consuming the sole green source

assertions: Driver matches W/G cost to flexible W/G and white-only sources without consuming the flexible source incorrectly.
limitations: Synthetic driver helper; does not submit a spell payment to the rules engine.

test.name: uses floating mana once and rejects insufficient colorless or generic resources

assertions: Driver spends three floating W for W plus two generic exactly once.
White mana cannot satisfy C; one W source cannot satisfy 2W plus generic.
limitations: No engine-side invalid-payment rollback or exact G/U/U scenario.

test.name: combines excess nontrample damage into one source-target allocation (first real-game regression)

assertions: Driver emits a single five-damage allocation to its only blocker.
limitations: Regression helper, not proof of a completed real-source game despite the test name.

test.name: trample distributes lethal first, then remaining power to the defender

assertions: Driver emits two to blocker and three to defender from a five-power trample domain.
limitations: Driver output only; no submitted damage command or source-state legality proof.

test.name: unowned decision is a driver failure rather than an invented pass

assertions: A missing owned decision causes driver failure.
limitations: Does not itself prove hidden state is unavailable to the driver.

test.name: durable exact retry survives close/reopen and a conflicting payload fails

assertions: Exact accepted command retry after native SQLite reopen returns original receipt and revision one.
Changed response under same command ID conflicts; one durable record remains and replay equals state.
limitations: Setup keep command only, not every decision type or browser OPFS.

test.name: serialized submissions deduplicate concurrent retries and reject stale/foreign actor without RNG advancement

assertions: Concurrent retries return same receipt once; stale revision and mismatched authenticated actor reject.
Current state/chance remains unchanged; projected library/opponent hand are absent.
Mutating returned current snapshot cannot mutate coordinator state.
limitations: Synthetic setup boundary in native SQLite.

test.name: real SQLite rollback at INSERT INTO commander_boundaries preserves state, receipt, events and retryability

assertions: Injected failure at INSERT INTO commander_boundaries returns PersistenceFailed and preserves prior in-memory and database state.
No receipt exists, one initial boundary remains; identical retry commits and replays to revision one.
limitations: Native SQLite adapter injection, not device-level disk loss or OPFS.

test.name: real SQLite rollback at UPDATE commander_matches preserves state, receipt, events and retryability

assertions: Injected failure at UPDATE commander_matches returns PersistenceFailed and preserves prior in-memory and database state.
No receipt exists, one initial boundary remains; identical retry commits and replays to revision one.
limitations: Native SQLite adapter injection, not device-level disk loss or OPFS.

test.name: real SQLite rollback at COMMIT preserves state, receipt, events and retryability

assertions: Injected failure at COMMIT returns PersistenceFailed and preserves prior in-memory and database state.
No receipt exists, one initial boundary remains; identical retry commits and replays to revision one.
limitations: Native SQLite adapter injection, not device-level disk loss or OPFS.

test.name: two native coordinators cannot overwrite a newer committed revision

assertions: Second writer with an old revision receives ConcurrentWrite; it keeps its old local snapshot and cannot append a second durable record.
limitations: Native SQLite optimistic writer conflict, not same-document OPFS ownership.

test.name: a pending casting/payment frame resumes and logical import replays before insertion

assertions: Payment continuation persists through native SQLite close/reopen and replay-validated logical import.
Resumed and imported payment commands yield identical receipts and states; importing over existing match rejects.
limitations: Zero-cost synthetic commander; not SET-03 bottom, PRI-03 response stack, CMD-03 owner choice or COM-07 durable distribution.

test.name: recomputed checkpoint checksum cannot hide a non-replayed state modification

assertions: A checkpoint tamper with a recomputed checksum is rejected by replay verification.
limitations: Single tamper case, not proof against arbitrary corrupted archives.

test.name: missing event boundary and altered request hash are detected

assertions: Missing event boundary and mismatched command request hash fail integrity verification.
limitations: Native SQLite corruption fixtures.

test.name: a durable retry refuses a receipt whose boundary was damaged while the coordinator was open

assertions: Receipt retry does not blindly return accepted after its durable boundary has been corrupted.
limitations: Native SQLite corruption fixture.

test.name: queued input is captured before the caller can mutate it

assertions: Submission captures caller input before subsequent mutation can alter queued command semantics.
limitations: One in-process queue case.

test.name: bad logical checksum, engine version and content/deck pins fail without importing

assertions: Logical checksum, incompatible engine and content/deck hash mismatch reject without inserting the match.
limitations: Native SQLite import rejection fixtures.

test.name: unrelated and future-version databases are refused without overwriting contents

assertions: Unrelated and newer-schema databases refuse initialization while preserving their contents.
limitations: Native SQLite schema guard only.

test.name: same pinned setup repeats physical cards and chance state; observations never expose any library or another hand

assertions: Repeated pinned four-seat setup produces equal state and chance cursor.
Every seat starts at 40 life, 7 hand and 92 library; each projection shows four commanders.
No observation includes a library object, another hand, or an unowned decision.
limitations: Synthetic 100-card decks, not a real-source deck or shuffle uniformity proof.
No post-mulligan privacy assertion or rules-authorized reveal case.

test.name: 2 seats collect mulligan declarations before redraw and enforce the correct first bottom count

assertions: No redraw occurs before all declarations in the first round.
First mulligan has 1 required bottom cards; next keep reaches upkeep.
limitations: One player redraws; broader multi-player and repeated rounds have separate tests.

test.name: 2 seats bottom every paid redraw before another mulligan declaration and keepers cannot rejoin

assertions: Three successive redraws bottom the required count before a next declaration.
Ordered selected card lineages become the ordered library tail; hand/library counts reflect each bottom.
Keep/mulligan during a required bottom is rejected with no state mutation.
Keepers retain their hands and cannot answer a later round; final keep starts upkeep.
limitations: Synthetic ordinary commands; does not reach the zero-card maximum or test pregame card effects.

test.name: 2 seats apply the proper starting-player draw rule

assertions: After all upkeep passes, first turn is main1 with seven cards.
limitations: Does not follow the second seat into their first draw or check the first-draw library count.

test.name: 4 seats collect mulligan declarations before redraw and enforce the correct first bottom count

assertions: No redraw occurs before all declarations in the first round.
First mulligan has 0 required bottom cards; next keep reaches upkeep.
limitations: One player redraws; broader multi-player and repeated rounds have separate tests.

test.name: 4 seats bottom every paid redraw before another mulligan declaration and keepers cannot rejoin

assertions: Three successive redraws bottom the required count before a next declaration.
Ordered selected card lineages become the ordered library tail; hand/library counts reflect each bottom.
Keep/mulligan during a required bottom is rejected with no state mutation.
Keepers retain their hands and cannot answer a later round; final keep starts upkeep.
limitations: Synthetic ordinary commands; does not reach the zero-card maximum or test pregame card effects.

test.name: 4 seats apply the proper starting-player draw rule

assertions: After all upkeep passes, first turn is draw with eight cards.
limitations: Does not follow the second seat into their first draw or check the first-draw library count.

test.name: four-seat paid redraws finish every bottom choice before the next declaration round

assertions: Two players take a free first mulligan and a paid second one.
Neither redraws before the second declaration round completes.
Both receive and answer a one-card bottom decision before either receives the next mulligan decision.
Both then keep six and setup reaches upkeep.
limitations: No simultaneous pregame abilities, zero-card boundary or post-redraw privacy assertions.

test.name: bad owner, malformed payload and illegal move leave state and chance untouched

assertions: Wrong actor, unknown command property and pass during mulligan are rejected.
Whole original state including chance remains equal.
limitations: Not every invalid response class is exercised here.

test.name: all three resolver modes preserve exact setup, decisions, staged casts, reversal, and transitions

assertions: Full scan, prepared scan and prepared indexed modes finish setup, stage/cancel a cast and advance 16 actions to equal normalized state.
limitations: Synthetic four-seat run; not full-source/all-query optimization certification.

test.name: resolver candidates track control, tap state, zone generations, and active timing exactly

assertions: All three modes discover the same creature and mana source.
Direct control, tap and zone mutations immediately change candidates even without an epoch advance.
Prepared modes run fewer exact checks than their finite universe in the fixture.
limitations: Constructed mutations test fresh views, not executable control-changing card programs.

test.name: canonical checkpoint round trips preserve candidate, observation, and transition ordering

assertions: All three modes preserve priority candidate and every seat observation ordering across canonical JSON round trip.
Twenty subsequent transitions equal uninterrupted state after repeated checkpoint restoration.
limitations: Synthetic passing/empty attack sequence; not Bun/browser or all-game replay parity.

test.name: announcement moves to stack before payment; cancellation restores exact object identity and command zone

assertions: Announcing a commander removes its original object and creates one stack object before the payment decision.
Cancellation restores original identity in command zone, clears stack and leaves commander cast count empty.
limitations: No modes, target multiplicity, division, trigger ordering or nonmana costs.

test.name: caster retains priority, all players pass, permanent resolves, then active player gets priority

assertions: A one-green commander is paid by the offered source; caster receives priority while the spell remains on stack.
One pass does not resolve; both seats passing resolves the permanent and active player gets priority.
Commander command-zone cast history increments to one.
limitations: Two seats and one creature only; no response spell, cast triggers, second/third commander tax or mana-ability negative assertion.

test.name: commander declines one graveyard SBA offer and receives another only after changing zones

assertions: Constructed graveyard entry produces an owner commander-zone decision.
Declining retains the graveyard object and ordinary passes do not repeat the offer.
A subsequent exile zone change produces a new offer.
limitations: Direct move establishes setup; no actual creature-death SBA, accepted move, dies trigger, or full simultaneous choice batch.

test.name: active player's loss does not begin another turn or give a dead player priority

assertions: A constructed active-player life total of zero is checked in a four-seat game.
Active identifier, turn and current step persist; departed player is lost, receives no decision, and game stays ongoing.
Object/seat invariants hold after removal.
limitations: Does not finish the departed player's turn, assert exact next seat, exercise foreign control history or stack-owner departure.

test.name: attack permissions, haste, vigilance, defender, and whole-declaration rollback

assertions: Eligible candidates include old untapped, vigilant and newly hasty creatures only.
Tapped vigilance, newly controlled nonhaste, defender, creature-battle and opponent creature are excluded.
Invalid mixed declaration does not tap any creature; accepted ordinary/vigilant attacks tap only the ordinary creature.
limitations: Direct combat functions on a constructed board; no full transition or priority/trigger continuation.

test.name: one attacker cannot attack twice or attack its controller

assertions: Duplicate attacker and self-defender choices throw; creature remains untapped.
limitations: Additional declaration restriction; not the complete COM-01 scenario.

test.name: four-seat blocking obeys defender ownership and APNAP with flying/reach

assertions: B then C own block decisions for attacks directed at each of them.
Out-of-order actor, ground-versus-flying and wrong defender assignments throw.
Newly controlled reach blocker may block without tapping, followed by C's block.
limitations: No planeswalker/battle protection, flying blocker against ground attacker, or post-declaration priority/trigger assertions.

test.name: menace rejects a single block, accepts two, and repeated blockers are invalid

assertions: One menace blocker is rejected without mutation; duplicate blocker is rejected; two distinct blockers accepted.
limitations: Supplementary source assertion beyond current COM-01..14 rows; does not cover general blocking requirements.

test.name: four-seat damage choices start at the actual active player and retain defender order

assertions: With C active, block and damage ownership follows C/D/B turn order as appropriate.
All four involved creatures receive two marked damage after completed assignments.
limitations: Constructed 2/2 combat variant, not COM-06's exact 3/3 fixture; does not run creature-death SBAs.

test.name: a first-strike blocker remains in combat after its attacker leaves

assertions: Removing the attacker does not remove its surviving first-strike blocker from combat.
First-strike participation remains present even though neither step has a target for damage.
limitations: A related boundary case; not COM-11's lethal blocker case or normal COM-14 no-extra-priority proof.

test.name: 5/5 may divide 2/3 between two 3/3 blockers, with simultaneous damage

assertions: Nontrample 5/5 can assign 2 and 3 to two 3/3 blockers without old damage ordering.
Damage cannot be applied until every owner assigns; before that no damage is marked.
Completed assignments mark 6/2/3 simultaneously; repeated apply does not apply damage twice.
No first-strike participant is detected.
limitations: Does not execute creature-death SBAs, full turn step advancement or intervening priority; COM-06 fixture differs.

test.name: trample allows lethal-plus-excess or all damage to blocker, not an underassignment

assertions: 1-to-blocker/4-to-player is rejected without mutation.
2/3 assignment deals three player damage.
All five to blocker is legal and leaves player life unchanged.
limitations: Does not assert subsequent blocker death or attacker damage.

test.name: trample lethal accounts for marked damage and deathtouch

assertions: One prior damage on a 2-toughness blocker reduces lethal assignment to one.
Deathtouch likewise makes one assigned to a 4-toughness blocker lethal.
Both 1/4 assignments deal four player damage; only deathtouch case marks that flag.
limitations: Does not execute deathtouch destruction/SBAs or assert indestructibility/prevention excess calculation.

test.name: leaving blocker preserves blocked status; trample can then reach defender

assertions: After direct blocker removal the attacker remains blocked.
Nontrample assigns/deals no player damage; trample may deal all two damage to player.
limitations: Removal is a fixture move, not an intervening cast/resolution.

test.name: first-strike snapshot prevents dealing again after losing first strike

assertions: Only first striker assigns first-step damage; attacker takes none then.
After constructed blocker removal and removal of first strike, historical participation prevents normal-step damage.
limitations: Blocker death and keyword change are direct fixture edits; no checkpoint or intervening priority is executed.

test.name: double strike applies two separate steps with a surviving blocker

assertions: First step marks two on blocker and zero on attacker.
Second step has both owners assign; cumulative marks are three on attacker and four on blocker.
limitations: Does not run death SBAs or actual priority between steps.

test.name: zero-power first striker still establishes the first-strike step

assertions: A zero-power first striker establishes first-strike step even with no positive assignment.
Only the ordinary blocker receives a later normal damage decision.
limitations: Related edge case, not full normal/first-strike turn orchestration.

test.name: wrong owner, foreign target, partial power, duplicate and fractional amounts cannot mutate state

assertions: Wrong owner, foreign target, partial power, fractional amount and duplicate pair are rejected.
Whole constructed state remains unchanged.
limitations: Direct function rejection; ordinary GameCommand validation is separate.

test.name: lifelink and incoming damage combine simultaneously; commander damage uses lineage

assertions: Lifelink and incoming damage combine before any SBA; defending life ends at two rather than temporarily losing.
Commander combat tally advances from 16 to 21 using physical lineage.
Deathtouch flag and damage on indestructible creature are marked.
limitations: Test explicitly stops before SBA: does not establish commander-damage elimination, noncombat exclusion or history across recasting.

test.name: pending compound damage choices survive schema serialization

assertions: Serialized RulesState with pending trample distribution resumes and applies identical assignments to equal final state.
limitations: JSON schema round trip only, not durable SQLite save/reload or Bun/browser parity.

test.name: COM-11 first-strike damage kills the blocker before normal damage and gives intervening priority

assertions: Ordinary attack/block commands expose intervening priority before advancing.
First-strike assignment through transition kills the 2/2 blocker at the real checkpoint; its new object is in graveyard and attacker has zero damage.
A then B receive priority during first-strike step; normal damage begins only after both pass.
Normal step deals no further damage; defender life remains 40 and only one combat damage event occurred.
limitations: Synthetic board and no triggers or abilities changing characteristics between steps.

approvedAssertions: Ordinary attack/block commands expose intervening priority before advancing.
First-strike assignment through transition kills the 2/2 blocker at the real checkpoint; its new object is in graveyard and attacker has zero damage.
A then B receive priority during first-strike step; normal damage begins only after both pass.
Normal step deals no further damage; defender life remains 40 and only one combat damage event occurred.

test.name: END-01 simultaneous lifelink and combat damage leave the defender alive at the real SBA checkpoint

assertions: Defender at four takes five unblocked damage while its blocker simultaneously deals three with lifelink.
First owner assignment changes no life; completed assignments plus checkpoint leave defender alive at two.
The 2/2 attacker dies through actual SBA, 3/3 blocker survives with two marked, and active player gets priority.
No player-loss event occurs.
limitations: Combat damage variant of END-01; does not exercise a spell lowering then restoring life during one resolution.

approvedAssertions: Defender at four takes five unblocked damage while its blocker simultaneously deals three with lifelink.
First owner assignment changes no life; completed assignments plus checkpoint leave defender alive at two.
The 2/2 attacker dies through actual SBA, 3/3 blocker survives with two marked, and active player gets priority.

test.name: COM-05 a blocker killed by a resolved spell leaves its nontrampling attacker blocked

assertions: Real cast/target/payment/pass commands resolve Sorin's Thirst during blocker priority and the real checkpoint moves the blocker to graveyard.
Attacker remains blocked; another full pass cycle advances directly to ordinary combat damage.
Nontrample deals no defender damage; trample may assign all two damage to defender, followed by active priority.
No first-strike StepStarted event occurs.
limitations: Each row runs the named trample variant; no prevention/replacement or attack triggers.

approvedAssertions: Real cast/target/payment/pass commands resolve Sorin's Thirst during blocker priority and the real checkpoint moves the blocker to graveyard.
Attacker remains blocked; another full pass cycle advances directly to ordinary combat damage.
Nontrample deals no defender damage; trample may assign all two damage to defender, followed by active priority.

test.name: COM-05 a blocker killed by a resolved spell leaves its trampling attacker blocked

assertions: Real cast/target/payment/pass commands resolve Sorin's Thirst during blocker priority and the real checkpoint moves the blocker to graveyard.
Attacker remains blocked; another full pass cycle advances directly to ordinary combat damage.
Nontrample deals no defender damage; trample may assign all two damage to defender, followed by active priority.
No first-strike StepStarted event occurs.
limitations: Each row runs the named trample variant; no prevention/replacement or attack triggers.

approvedAssertions: Real cast/target/payment/pass commands resolve Sorin's Thirst during blocker priority and the real checkpoint moves the blocker to graveyard.
Attacker remains blocked; another full pass cycle advances directly to ordinary combat damage.
Nontrample deals no defender damage; trample may assign all two damage to defender, followed by active priority.

test.name: PRI-04 immediate mana activation resets prior passes before stack resolution

assertions: With a spell pending after A and B passed, C activates a Swamp and retains priority with one floating black mana.
C,D,A passes leave the spell pending; only B completing the fresh four-seat cycle resolves it.
Floating mana survives passes and resolution, then clears when the next phase begins.
limitations: One immediate intrinsic land mana ability; no triggered/restricted mana.

approvedAssertions: With a spell pending after A and B passed, C activates a Swamp and retains priority with one floating black mana.
C,D,A passes leave the spell pending; only B completing the fresh four-seat cycle resolves it.
Floating mana survives passes and resolution, then clears when the next phase begins.

test.name: END-05 active player loses from a resolved draw and the turn finishes cleanup before the next living turn

assertions: Empty library alone leaves A alive; casting and resolving Inspiration targeting A causes the real failed-draw SBA loss.
All A-owned objects leave, while active identifier A, main phase and turn five continue with priority B.
All subsequent decisions before turn end belong to survivors; cleanup event for turn five precedes B untapping for turn six.
Next stable decision is B upkeep priority, not a skipped immediate new turn at the moment of loss.
limitations: No foreign control history, dead-player resolution choice, departed-seat skip on a later complete rotation, or exceptional cleanup trigger.

test.name: twelve deterministic composition fixtures preserve count, singleton, color and source-release hashes

assertions: Twelve synthetic deck fixtures are distinct and deterministic.
Each has 100 cards, 61 singleton entry rows, correct computed deck hash and successful engine admission.
limitations: No negative 99/101, duplicate-name or color-identity fixture; no basic-land production restriction assertion.
Synthetic release: not source-card certification or twelve completed games.

test.name: spell deck profiles retain seven pinned programs, legal 100-card composition, and 39 basics

assertions: Two additional deck fixtures total 100, have 19 plus 20 basic lands, unique definition entry rows and successful admission.
Together they include all seven reviewed spell names with expected source version hashes.
Removing Divination rejects the dependent fixture.
limitations: Filler creatures are synthetic; not all-card semantic certification or a completed full game.

test.name: tampered releases and missing composition dependencies fail explicitly

assertions: Tampered release hash and missing required basic land definition reject fixture generation.
limitations: Does not validate all source legality or recipe semantics.

postImplementationReviews.scope: COM-11 plain first-strike death and intervening priority; COM-05 resolved removal with/without trample; END-01 simultaneous combat lifelink survival; PRI-04 immediate mana action resets passes. This does not certify entire scenarios, groups, or cards.
